stories.title: Oura may soon use a wearable patch to screen for positional sleep apnea
stories.excerpt: Oura’s patented concept now looks more focused on distinguishing obstructive sleep apnea from central sleep apnea. A newly granted Oura patent details how a wearable patch could combine blood oxygen tracking with body position sensing to screen for positional sleep apnea.

stories.title: Apple patent details multi-wearable sensor fusion for improved health tracking
stories.excerpt: A new Apple patent describes a system that could combine health data from multiple wearables to produce a single, more accurate reading. Apple may be working to make wearable health tracking more accurate by having several devices check the same signal at the same time.

stories.title: Oura's patent reveals how future smart rings could track blood pressure
stories.excerpt: The company is still pushing toward one of wearables’ toughest goals: meaningful blood pressure tracking without a cuff. Oura may soon estimate blood pressure metrics by analyzing the subtle wave shapes of multi-wavelength optical sensors.

stories.title: Samsung update brings faster Sleep Coaching and Strava integration to Galaxy Watch
stories.excerpt: Samsung has announced a major update to its Health app, lowering the barrier to entry for its Sleep Coaching program while adding deeper Strava routing and expanded training tiers for runners. Previously requiring seven days of tracked sleep logged within a month to get started, Samsung Health v.6.24 lets users start Sleep Coaching with just three days of data collected over a two-week window.

stories.title: Strava takes on fitness apps with coach-led strength workouts and rep tracking
stories.excerpt: Strava is launching native, coach-led strength workouts directly within its mobile app, offering guided exercise animations and live set-and-rep tracking that syncs straight to athletes' Workout Logs. Rolling out to subscribers over the coming weeks—with a sample workout unlocked for free users—the update aims to remove friction from gym-based strength training.

stories.title: Whoop’s plans for fit monitoring could solve wearable tech’s biggest problem
stories.excerpt: Whoop may be working on a system to resolve an issue that can undermine the data accuracy of even the very best screenless trackers—wearing it incorrectly. In a patent filing in the United States, Whoop explains a system that would measure the tightness of the device when worn on multiple areas of the body, and report back with findings on necessary adjustments.

stories.title: Garmin's $2,500 MARQ Gen 3 collection adds LTE and a Commander edition
stories.excerpt: Four years after Gen 2, Garmin’s tool watches return with bigger AMOLED screens, built-in satellite SOS, and leakproof buttons Garmin has announced the third generation of its luxury MARQ smartwatch collection, introducing six Grade-5 titanium tool watches equipped with larger displays, standalone LTE inReach connectivity, and built-in voice capabilities.

stories.title: The best stress relief device: Our top picks designed to help you unwind
stories.excerpt: We’ve looked at the top stress relief devices on the market—here’s what you need to knowThere are many ways to... There are many ways to manage stress, and the 2026 health tech market offers a growing range of devices designed to help. From ear-based wearables that target the vagus nerve to wrist-worn devices that may help you stay grounded in the moment—there’s a lot to choose from.

stories.title: Garmin has a story to tell—and MARQ Gen 3 is where it puts on the tuxedo
stories.excerpt: Wareable sits down with Garmin's Todd Register to talk about the launch of the MARQ Gen 3 When I last sat down with Todd Register, Garmin’s Creative Lead for Outdoors, it was in Lisbon, Portugal, for the launch of MARQ Gen 2.

stories.title: Fitbit Edge arrives to bridge the gap between Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air
stories.excerpt: Succeeding the Charge 6, the lightweight aluminum tracker packs a 46% larger screen, upgraded GPS, and modular repairability Google has officially launched the Fitbit Edge, a $179.99 fitness tracker designed for users who want rich daily health metrics without the size or price tag of a fully-featured smartwatch.
